svg.text: The 5 Secondary Āvāzes: Branching Architecture from Dastgāh-e Shūr
Empirical Analysis Across 18,632 Note Strikes & Modal Mechanics (Īst, Shāhed, Motaghayyer Shifts)
TRUNK: DASTGĀH-E SHŪR
The Mother System (Umm al-Maqāmāt):
Two symmetrical Dāng-e Shūr [S + S] joined by 9/8 tone:
Do (Tonic / Īst) [0¢]
Re-koron (Attr) [139¢]
Mi-flat [294¢]
Fa (Top Dāng 1) [498¢]
Sol (Panjgāh) [702¢]
La-koron (Qaracheh) [841¢]
Si-flat (Razavi) [996¢]
Do (Octave) [1200¢]
Empirical Strike Corpus (5 Āvāzes):
• Total Analyzed Strikes: 18,632 strikes
• Canonical Radif Tracks: 89 tracks
• Masters: Borumand, Karimi, Shahnazi,
Hormozi, Alizadeh, Saba, Ebadi, Kasaei
Branching Mechanism:
Each Āvāz preserves the core fretboard of
Shūr, but completely reorganizes its musical
hierarchy via Īst, Shāhed, or Motaghayyer.
1. ĀVĀZ-E ABŪ'ATĀ
Shift: Melodic Focal Center (Shāhed) → 2nd Degree (Re-koron, +139¢)
Kernel Formula: Do (Īst / Pedestal) ↔ Reᵏ (Shāhed / Axis) ↔ Mi♭ (Peak)
While resting on Do, the entire melodic energy revolves around Re-koron. Movement leaps between Do and Mi♭ through Reᵏ w
ith characteristic undulating motifs (Sayakhi, Ramkali, Hejāz). In Hejāz, the mode climbs to the 5th (Sol) with a dramat
ic shift to Dāng-e Chahārgāh/Homāyūn flavor.
Empirical Corpus: 3,345 strikes across 21 tracks (Shahnazi, Karimi, Forutan)
2. ĀVĀZ-E BAYĀT-E TORK (BAYĀT-E ZAND)
Shift: Resting Tone (Īst) & Focal Center (Shāhed) → 3rd Degree (Mi-flat, +294¢)
Kernel Formula: Mi♭ (Primary Īst & Shāhed) | Fa (Peak) | Do (Lower Root / Final Foroud)
By treating Mi♭ as the principal resting tone, Bayāt-e Tork produces a warm, major-like spiritual resonance despite shar
ing Shūr frets. Famously used in the Iranian Adhān (by Rahim Moazenzadeh) and Sufi cantillation (Masnavi, Rowh al-Arvāh)
. The lower Do acts as an occasional solemn anchor.
Empirical Corpus: 2,034 strikes across 16 tracks (Borumand Mirza Abdollah Vol 2, Karimi, Shahnazi)
3. ĀVĀZ-E AFSHĀRĪ
Shift: Tonal Axis → 4th (Fa) & 5th (Sol) with Dynamic Variable Degree (Motaghayyer)
Kernel Formula: Fa (Primary Īst) | Sol ↔ Solᵏ / Fa♯ (Motaghayyer) | Do (Final Foroud)
Afshārī possesses one of the most poignant emotional signatures. The melody hovers around Fa and Sol, but the 5th degree
is motaghayyer: in descending cadences it is pulled flat into Sol-koron (~640¢-660¢), creating an agonizing, unresolved
tension before releasing into lower Shūr.
Empirical Corpus: 4,278 strikes across 16 tracks (Hormozi private setār, Borumand, Karimi, Shahnazi)
4. ĀVĀZ-E DASHTĪ
Shift: Focal Center (Shāhed) → 5th/6th Degree (Sol / La-koron) + Bimodal Motaghayyer
Kernel Formula: Do (Lower Root) | Sol (Pedestal) | Laᵏ (Shāhed / Climax) | Solᵏ (Variable)
The quintessential mode of Persian pastoral longing ('the crying of the desert'). Melody ascends rapidly through Dāng 1
to obsessively circle La-koron. In Deylamān and Ouj, the 5th degree drops microtonally into Sol-koron, forming an expres
sive weeping motif unmatched in Mediterranean modal music.
Empirical Corpus: 6,671 strikes across 27 tracks (Shahnazi, Karimi, Alizadeh, Saba, Lotfi, Ebadi)
5. BAYĀT-E KORD
Shift: Re-anchored to Shūr Tonic (Do) with Prolonged Neutral 2nd Tension (Re-koron)
Kernel Formula: Do (Persistent Īst) | Reᵏ (Dramatic Mordent / Sustained Focus) | Mi♭ (Transient)
Closely aligned with Dashtī and Shūr, Bayāt-e Kord retains the lower Do as its rigid resting point but treats the neutra
l second (Reᵏ, 13/12) with intense prolonged emphasis and rapid rhythmic mordents. Melodic lines rarely climb beyond the
fourth (Fa), creating an austere, meditative chamber atmosphere.
Empirical Corpus: 2,304 strikes across 9 tracks (Borumand Mirza Abdollah Vol 2 complete, Alizadeh Ocora)
